claims.text: The initial PtPdRhRuIrOs catalyst is a uniformly mixed solid solution with a low density of surface defects.
A mild reductive plasma treatment can increase the surface defect density of nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs.
Controlled thermal annealing can increase the surface defect density of nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs.
Increasing surface defect density produces more undercoordinated metal sites.
Undercoordinated sites alter the surface electronic structure.
A higher density of defect sites creates a broader distribution of adsorption energies for ethanol and its intermediates.
Changing adsorption energies can improve reactant and intermediate adsorption/desorption dynamics.
Improved adsorption/desorption dynamics will increase catalytic turnover for ethanol oxidation.
The defect-enriched catalyst will have a lower ethanol-oxidation onset potential than the untreated catalyst.
The defect-enriched catalyst will have a higher ethanol-oxidation turnover frequency than the untreated catalyst.
The proposed effect should hold from 25 to 80 °C under typical ethanol-oxidation electrolytes and controlled electrochemical potentials.
TEM and XPS can quantify the surface defect density sufficiently to verify the intervention.
The magnitude and precise dependence of catalytic performance on defect type and density are uncertain.

contradictions.description: Failure of the treatment to measurably increase defect density is treated as falsification, but it would instead indicate failure of the intended intervention and would not test whether an actual defect-density increase changes activity.
